title: Five Platforms, One Field
description: How The Playground, BuildLang, The Flywheel, The Commons, and Research connect into one verified architecture with live benchmarks and datasets.
lede: Every engine, compiler, verification tool, civic reader, and open dataset now builds toward one connected stack: write deterministic code, render and measure physical light, verify every claim with offline receipts, and publish the results with open data.
sub: Start with any platform below to run it on your own machine, inspect how outputs flow across repositories, or read the observed benchmark numbers and open gaps.

platforms.title: The Playground
platforms.what: A deterministic rendering engine and multi-medium creative suite. One seed produces images, living type, plotter lines, sound, and 3D worlds, while the native C++ Direct3D 12, Vulkan, and WebGPU renderer checks real-time lighting passes against ray-traced and path-traced references.
platforms.consumes: Bit-exact BuildLang math kernels, measured spectral material tables, and DS-03/DS-04 regression benchmarks.
platforms.produces: Deterministic multi-medium renders, Low Water 3D game scenes, Estuary interactive fields, and canonical engine-receipt/1 verification envelopes.
platforms.contract: engine-receipt/1 SHA-256 verification envelopes plus superstack.receipt/1 visual and audio hashes.
parts: Superframe
Core multi-medium engine, marbled surfaces, Estuary Lantern, and consolidated colour, signal, and archive packages.
RAW DX12 & Native
Direct3D 12, Vulkan, and WebGPU renderer with RayQuery GI/RTAO, volumetric clouds, fluid fire/water, and 36 debug views.
Low Water
Five-era narrative game built as the engine's full-scale world and lighting proof.
286 Formulas & Colour
Known-answer optics, colour science (build-color), signal kernels, and 91 executable IEEE-754 calibration kernels.

platforms.title: BuildLang
platforms.what: A compiled systems language whose function types declare every external capability they touch (files, network, C FFI). The compiler checks laws beside the code, emits deterministic C, HLSL, and GLSL, and hosts its own embedded SQL database (BDB), module universe, editor grammars, and RISC-V/OS experiments.
platforms.consumes: Typed source modules, DS-02 compiler and porting suites, and SQL logic test corpora.
platforms.produces: Repeatable native binaries, bit-exact parallel reductions (par_for), embedded BDB stores, and verified kernels for The Playground.
platforms.contract: Declared effect-row manifests, repeatable SHA-256 build hashes, and C translation validation.
parts: buildc 1.15.0
Algebraic effect rows, checked pure par_for/par_map, offline package lockfiles, and repeatable C/shader codegen.
BDB (BuildDB)
Pure BuildLang embedded SQL engine with crash-recovery and cross-process rollback tests.
Universe & Suite
267 module files in universe/, five consolidated Build suite libraries in suite/, and editor syntax packages in editors/.
RISC-V & OS
emu-rv64 emulator and bare-metal scheduler experiments (os-pfa, os-runq).

platforms.verified: 25 November 2026: buildlang v1.15.0 on GitHub and crates.io; 147/147 repeatable build hashes and 5.3x to 5.9x bit-exact par_for speedup; honest gap recorded: 195 of 267 universe/ files still fail buildc check (tracked in buildlang #290).

platforms.title: The Flywheel & Articulate
platforms.what: A self-hosted AI workstation, coding harness, and accountability platform for any hosted or local model. Thirty previously separate tools now live in one tree, recording every step as a signed offline receipt, enforcing Three-Plate independent verification, and checking outbound prose with Articulate (ARTIQL8).
platforms.consumes: Model outputs, engine-receipt/1 bundles from The Playground, build hashes from BuildLang, and claim threads from The Commons.
platforms.produces: Signed Merkle receipts (MATCH, DRIFT, or UNVERIFIABLE), Three-Plate audit verdicts, Articulate prose checks, and live Bulletin logs.
platforms.contract: Offline-recheckable JSON receipts, Three-Plate proposer/mutator/oracle checks, and zero-mutation protected spans.
parts: Core Harness (v2.0.0)
Runs models behind one local interface with cryptographic step receipts and offline verification.
30 Consolidated Packages
Canon, Mneme, Forum, Crucible, Gather, EMET, Index, Plexus, Relay, Chorus, Learn, Bulletin, and safety utilities under packages/.
Three-Plate Verification
Separates proposer, independent hypothesis mutator plus secret-prefix scanner, and execution ground-truth oracle.
Articulate (ARTIQL8)
v0.19.1 local prose checker (2,096 passing tests) flagging hedging, filler, and register drift without rewriting author facts.
platforms.run: pip install flywheel-verify articulate-writing && flywheel up
platforms.verified: 25 November 2026: flywheel v2.0.0 (flywheel-verify) and articulate v0.19.1 (articulate-writing) live on GitHub and PyPI; 30 consolidated packages wired under flywheel/packages/ and demos/.

platforms.title: The Commons
platforms.what: A local-first browser extension and cross-domain knowledge archive that inspects public claims in place. It shows where linked sources come from, surfaces coordination patterns and fact-check reviews, and decomposes saved posts into parts (words, media, replies) for longitudinal study.
platforms.consumes: Public web threads, linked domain provenance records, fact-check feeds, and multi-modal reference saves.
platforms.produces: In-page provenance panels, structured post decompositions, and the 43,380-item cross-domain knowledge graph feeding Research.
platforms.contract: Local-only processing with source-hash citations and zero server tracking of browsing activity.
parts: CMMNS Extension (v3.10.0)
Inspects sources, coordination cues, and published fact-checks directly in Chrome, Edge, Brave, or Firefox.
43K Cross-Domain Archive
27,678 unique text records, 7,957 reviewed stills, and 2,907 video motion contact sheets distilled into structural laws.
Civic Provenance & Radar
Links domain ownership and published reviews directly to primary sources without opaque scores.

platforms.title: Research & Datasets
platforms.what: Preregistered investigations, peer-comparable benchmarks, and seven oracle-backed datasets compiled from real engineering runs. Null results, falsified hypotheses, and open estimator limits are published beside positive findings.
platforms.consumes: Verified outputs from all four engineering platforms, preregistered timestamps, and controlled planted-failure traps.
platforms.produces: Seven scrubbed benchmark datasets (DS-01 to DS-07), 16 Zenodo DOIs and site papers, and cross-domain structural laws.
platforms.contract: SHA-256 checksummed dataset manifests, planted wrong-control tests, and explicit Verified lines on every publication.
parts: Seven Datasets (DS-01..DS-07)
7,065 verified JSONL rows covering agent tool repair, BuildLang compiler bench, 286 physics/colour equations, RAW motion specs, Commons graph, planted-failure traps, and recall bench.
Preregistered Findings
669 recorded laboratory findings and timestamped preregistrations where nulls stay public.
16 Papers & Preprints
Public PDFs and Zenodo DOIs covering verifiable trust, capability effects, faithfulness conservation, and bounded verification.

honestGaps: Numbers that have not passed yet stay marked as open gaps. In BuildLang, 195 of 267 universe/ modules still fail buildc check (1 lex, 21 parse, 173 type errors) and BDB still needs page-level checksums to close silent fuzz corruption. In DS-03, 91 of 286 equation specs have executable float64 kernels while 195 remain specification-only and 12 discrepancies are flagged. In DS-07 recall, 7 of 80 held-out queries still miss top-5 across memories and sessions. In audio stem separation, current htdemucs_ft baseline (9.03 dB SDR) trails BS-RoFormer (11.99 dB) by 2.96 dB. In RAW, WebGPU browser scenes run on a subset of the native DX12 pass stack.
